rationale: Add a custom job timeout (10 minutes) to bound runaway CI consumption. The workflow currently has no timeout, so a hung configure/make/check step could run until the GitHub-hosted runner default (6 hours). Historical runs complete in ~2-3 minutes (per CI history), so 10 minutes provides ample headroom for cold starts and slower runners while still capping pathological cases. This directly applies pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, which has experimental evidence showing 26.8% elapsed-time savings on a measured fork (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) and a literature-reported VM-time reduction of 12.9% (free) / 8.1% (paid). No other pattern fits: the build uses system packages (no language-package cache to leverage), the matrix covers distinct platforms where all outcomes are likely required (contraindicating fail-fast), and cancel-in-progress is already enabled.
